title: An abelian subvariety of a connected group is central
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Group schemes and homomorphisms are as in [def-sc-group-scheme], closed subgroups as in [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], smoothness as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], connectedness as in [def-weil-connected-scheme], and finite type as in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Dimensions mean topological Krull dimensions [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $G$ be a smooth connected separated finite-type $k$-group scheme and let $i:A\hookrightarrow G$ be a closed subgroup scheme with $A$ an abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety], that is, proper, smooth and connected over $k$. Then for every commutative $k$-algebra $B$, every $a\in A(B)$ and every $g\in G(B)$ one has $i(a)g=gi(a)$ in $G(B)$. In particular, $A$ is a central, hence normal, subgroup scheme of $G$. No affineness, properness or commutativity hypothesis is imposed on $G$.

source.place: Corollary 8.13, p.151, applied to an abelian subvariety (Definition 8.15); anti-affineness of complete connected group varieties is stated before Proposition 8.12. Independent of Proposition 8.25. No Stacks tag states this centrality result.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-abelian-variety-characterization] to the proper smooth connected group scheme $A/k$. It gives that $A$ is geometrically integral; hence its base change to every extension field is reduced and irreducible, in particular connected. Thus $A$ is geometrically reduced and geometrically connected, as required by the rigidity lemma.

source.place: Tags 04KV (varieties-lemma-geometrically-connected-if-connected-and-point), 0B7Q (groupoids-lemma-connected-group-scheme-over-field-irreducible), and 0BFC (groupoids-lemma-abelian-variety-smooth), as recorded in the cited characterization.

proof.text: Using multiplication, inverse, the subgroup homomorphism $i$, and the projections, form the $k$-morphism $c:A\times_kG\to G$ given on points by $c(a,g)=i(a)g\,i(a)^{-1}g^{-1}$. The group identities give $c|_{A\times\{e_G\}}=e_G$ and $c|_{\{e_A\}\times G}=e_G$ as morphisms: the two expressions reduce respectively to $i(a)i(a)^{-1}$ and $gg^{-1}$. These identities hold as diagrams of schemes, including after arbitrary base change.

source.place: Theorem 1.1 (Rigidity), printed pp.8–9: the two coordinate axes; application to the commutator morphism.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-rigidity] with $X=A$, $Y=G$, $Z=G$, $f=c$, and $y_0=e_G\in G(k)$. Properness of $A$ is a hypothesis, and Step 1 gives its geometric connectedness and reducedness. The parameter scheme $G$ is connected, the target $G$ is separated and locally of finite type, and Step 2 contracts the fibre at the rational point $e_G$. Therefore there is a morphism $h:G\to G$ such that $c=h\circ\operatorname{pr}_2$. Pull back this equality along the section $s:G\to A\times_kG$, $s(g)=(e_A,g)$. Since $\operatorname{pr}_2\circ s=\mathrm{id}_G$ and $c\circ s=e_G$, one obtains $h=e_G$ and hence $c=e_G$ as morphisms of schemes.

source.place: Theorem 1.1, printed pp.8–9; the factorization form is the statement of the existing blueprint rigidity lemma.

proof.text: For any commutative $k$-algebra $B$, evaluate the morphism identity $c=e_G$ on $(a,g)\in A(B)\times G(B)$. It gives $i(a)g\,i(a)^{-1}g^{-1}=1$. Multiplying first on the right by $g$ and then by $i(a)$ gives $i(a)g=gi(a)$. Thus $i(A(B))$ is central in $G(B)$ for every $B$. Moreover $g\,i(a)g^{-1}=i(a)$, so conjugation preserves the subgroup for every $B$, which is normality in [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup].

source.place: Theorem 1.1, printed pp.8–9, applied to the commutator; final group-identity calculation.

proof_origin.place: Application of Theorem 1.1, printed pp.8–9, in the factorization form of lem-sc-rigidity, to the mixed commutator A × G → G. This proves the conclusion of Milne Algebraic Groups Corollary 8.13 for an abelian subvariety.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q107-a1151dc44 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item in full. Only the item record changed; there are no new nodes. The statement is mathematically the same as on the base and is true: Milne, Algebraic Groups (iAG2017) p.151, Cor 8.13, together with the paragraph before Prop 8.12 (a complete connected group variety is anti-affine). It is not weakened. Step 1: lem-sc-abelian-variety-characterization says A is geometrically integral, which gives the geometrically reduced and connected hypotheses rigidity needs. Step 2: the commutator c=i(a)g i(a)^-1 g^-1 is a scheme morphism, and both axis restrictions are the constant e_G; this is elementary. Step 3: lem-sc-rigidity, both the old text and the blueprint_update. Every hypothesis holds: A proper, G connected, G separated, and the fibre at the rational point e_G maps to a single point. Rigidity gives c=h∘pr2; precomposing with (e_A,id) gives h=e_G, so c=e_G. This matches the mechanism of Milne, Abelian Varieties, Thm 1.1, pp.8-9. Step 4: evaluating c=e_G on B-points gives centrality, and normality as defined in def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup. Edge cases checked: trivial A, G=A, G=A×SL2, and non-reduced B (covered by the morphism equality). A DAG scan found no duplicate. lem-sfb-conjugation-finite-jet-kernel needs affine G and is correctly not used. The two off-unit citations, lem-sc-rigidity and lem-sc-abelian-variety-characterization, are generic black-box tools; I accept both tool_uses. No SGA is cited.

lean.statement: theorem abelianSubvariety_central {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (G A : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GrpObj G] [GrpObj A] [Smooth G.hom] [ConnectedSpace G.left] [IsSeparated G.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] [QuasiCompact G.hom] [IsAbelianVariety A] (i : A ⟶ G) [IsClosedSubgroupScheme i] : (∀ (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (a : Over.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k B))) ⟶ A) (g : Over.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k B))) ⟶ G), (a ≫ i) * g = g * (a ≫ i)) ∧ IsNormalSubgroupScheme i

reviewed_lean.note: Only the item lean field changed; the statement is verbatim in AbelianSubvarietyCentral.lean, with a sorry proof. Clause by clause against the node: k field + IsAlgClosed; G,A in Over(Spec k) with GrpObj; Smooth/ConnectedSpace/IsSeparated/LocallyOfFiniteType+QuasiCompact on G (the finite-type record convention); IsAbelianVariety A = proper+smooth+connected; IsClosedSubgroupScheme i = IsMonHom + R-point injectivity + closed immersion (def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup record). Conclusion: for all B:Type u k-algebras and points a,g, (a≫i)*g = g*(a≫i), with Hom.group consistent with IsMonHom.monoidHom; plus IsNormalSubgroupScheme i. No extra assumptions on G (affine/proper/commutative/dimension). Edge cases: trivial A, A=G, A×SL2, nonreduced or zero B, all characteristics; universes consistent. Provable via exists_eq_snd_comp (Rigidity.lean:335) + IsAbelianVariety.geometricallyIntegral. Docstrings carry Milne AG Cor 8.13/Def 8.15, AV Thm 1.1, the blueprint id and all four proof steps. No duplicate declaration, no new defs, no competing S2 delivery. Not recompiled (no change).
